items.title: Mock 1 — Reorder Paragraphs Q1 (False memories)
paragraphs: False memories are constructed by combining actual memories with the content of suggestions received from others. During the process, individuals may forget the source of the information.
This is a classic example of source confusion, in which the content and the source become dissociated.
Of course, because we can implant false childhood memories in some individuals in no way implies that all memories that arise after suggestion are necessarily false.
Put another way, although experimental work on the creation of false memories may raise doubt about the validity of long-buried memories, such as repeated trauma, it in no way disproves them.

items.title: Mock 1 — Reorder Paragraphs Q2 (Plant and Protein)
paragraphs: Researchers found that proteins can regulate plant growth by coordinating various biological responses.
They discovered that these specific proteins trigger mechanisms that allow plants to conserve water during environmental stress.
Understanding this process helps researchers find that some grains can live in drought conditions that would typically be fatal.
In the future, this can be applied to crops so they can adapt to drought, potentially resolving the global food crisis or issues of human hunger.
